We are preparing a short RFP and want to include realistic expectations. If you can send a short matrix of options and any sample APIs or runbooks, that would be helpful.

Hi Jennifer — thanks for the clear list. Summary below and I attached a concise matrix (data_retention_matrix_v2.xlsx) that maps options to compliance needs. High-level answers:

1) Residency: Hosted API (multi-region) and Dedicated (region pinned) both support US-only deployment. For the tightest controls we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) which gives you full network control and KMS integration.

2) Retention limits: Configurable per-tenant and per-route. Default hosted retention is 30 days for inputs and 90 days for logs/metrics; we can set hard caps down to 0 days for inputs (immediate discard) and as low as 7 days for operational logs. For Dedicated/Private customers we offer contractual retention SLAs and tooling to enforce X-day limits (we'll put concrete numbers in the matrix).

3) Deletion APIs & proof: We have tenant-level and object-level deletion APIs and an audit log that records deletion events (timestamp, requestor, object id). We can produce deletion reports and signed deletion certificates on request — common for procurement and SOC reviews.

4) Redaction options: - Client-side redaction prior to ingestion (recommended for PHI) - Server-side rule-based entity redaction (PII detection + remove/replace) - Deterministic hashing for identifiers when needed (pseudonymization) - Attachment handling: we support text extraction and configurable redaction pipelines for PDFs/Docs; for images we can strip metadata and run OCR redaction flows. I attached a diagram (redaction_options_diagram.png) with workflow variants.

Next steps I propose: a 45-min technical deep-dive where Rishi can walk your engineers through APIs and run a live deletion proof on a test tenant. Neha will coordinate procurement questions and the SOW draft.

If that sounds good I'll kick off a calendar invite.

Best,

Hi Mark / Jennifer — technical clarifications below (working off Hannah's summary and the attached matrix).

- Deletion certificates: Our deletion API returns an operation id and audit log entry. We can provide a signed PDF containing the operation id, UTC timestamp, target object ids (hashed), and an operational signature from our infra team. The audit log contains immutable entries for create/read/delete with requestor identity (OID).

- Backup behavior: Backups are configurable per-deployment. For hosted customers there is a standard backup retention of 14 days; for Dedicated/Private we can set backup retention to a customer maximum (including 0-day backups) and restrict snapshot access. We can include a clause in the SOW to limit backups for CuraHealth to 7 days or less.

- Immediate deletion vs tombstone: We support both immediate physical deletion (best effort for private deployments) and logical deletion/tombstone for analytic replication pipelines. For compliance, we recommend: ingest -> optional server-side redaction -> store ephemeral -> commit to model logs for N days (configurable) -> permanent delete (API triggered). For hosted flows where caches (KV cache) are used, we have explicit KV invalidation APIs — these are part of the deletion operation.

- Redaction primitives we support: entity-based removal (NER filter), token masking (retain token count but replace tokens), deterministic hashing (consistent pseudonym), and schema-based filtering (remove fields from structured events). We can run redaction at three points: client-side (best), ingestion-time pre-store, and post-process batch redaction.

- Attachments: text-based docs go through the same pipeline. For binary attachments we surface a processing log showing which pages/regions were redacted.

I can prepare a short runbook that includes sample API calls (DELETE /v1/tenants/{tid}/data/{object_id}, POST /v1/tenants/{tid}/deletion-run) and an example deletion-certificate template. If you want, I can also run a deletion exercise against a sandbox tenant during the call.

Thanks,
